vc-van.title: Miami Vice City Small-Group Tour
vc-van.desc: Our signature tour, by day or by night. Take a daytime departure, or the sunset + night run that starts at golden hour and finishes as the neon switches on. The spots that inspired eight trailer scenes, in one loop: the Ocean Drive neon, the Venetian Causeway, downtown, the Wynwood murals, Little Haiti, Little Havana and the Brickell skyline.

vc-car.title: Private Classic Convertible Tour
vc-car.desc: The most cinematic way to see it. Just your crew in a top-down vintage convertible with a driver-guide who knows every angle. Same stops as the signature tour, at your pace.
incl: Golden-hour photo stop on the causeway
Pickup in Miami Beach, Downtown or Brickell

vc-jeep.title: Private Jeep Convertible Tour
vc-jeep.desc: Roof off, wind in. Your crew in an open-top Jeep with a driver-guide, running the full Miami loop from the Ocean Drive neon to the Brickell skyline.
incl: Pickup in Miami Beach, Downtown or Brickell

vc-boat.title: Miami Vice City by Boat
vc-boat.desc: Our Millionaire’s Row cruise. Loop out of Bayside past PortMiami, Fisher Island and the Miami Beach Marina megayachts, then the celebrity mansions of Star, Palm and Hibiscus Islands and the Venetian Islands, before a golden-hour hold on the skyline.
good: Pairs well with the city tour

airboat.title: Grasslands Airboat
airboat.desc: Leave the neon behind for the swamp that inspired the game’s wetlands. Round-trip shuttle from Miami, then an airboat run through the Everglades sawgrass with a wildlife guide. Add an alligator farm visit, or stay for a glow-in-the-dark ATV ride after sunset.
good: A half day outside the city

keys.title: Leonida Keys Road Trip
keys.desc: The island road that inspired the game’s Keys. Drive the Overseas Highway through Key Largo and Islamorada to the Seven Mile Bridge, with beach time and a seafood lunch stop.
incl: Beach time at a state park

pass.title: Leonida City Pass
pass.desc: The Miami Vice City small-group tour, Miami Vice City by Boat and the Grasslands Airboat, booked on your own schedule. A $237 value for $199.

vicecity.name: Miami Vice City
vicecity.blurb: Neon hotels, glass towers, murals and the bay: the real city that inspired the game. Ride it in a small group, privately, or by boat.

grassrivers.name: Grasslands
grassrivers.blurb: Sawgrass to the horizon, airboats, gators and quiet water: the wetlands that inspired the game’s swamp scenes. An hour from Miami.

keys.name: Leonida Keys
keys.blurb: Island roads, turquoise water and bridges that run to the horizon. A full-day road trip down the island chain.

ambrosia.name: Lake Okeechobee
ambrosia.blurb: Sugar country, heat-haze roads and small-town stops. We’re scouting this route for 2027.

LAND.name: Ocean Drive
LAND.p: Meet on the Art Deco strip the first trailer’s look is built on: pastel hotels, neon signage and the Clevelander corner.
LAND.np: We finish here after dark, when the whole strip glows pink and blue, exactly like the trailer.

LAND.name: Lummus Park Beach
LAND.p: The candy-colored lifeguard towers and the sand from the beach scenes. Crew photo stop.
LAND.np: Golden-hour light on the lifeguard towers: the best crew photo of the night.

LAND.name: Venetian Causeway
LAND.p: Island-hop across the bay on the old drawbridge causeway, skyline rising ahead.

LAND.name: Downtown & Biscayne Blvd
LAND.p: The waterfront arena, the color-changing crown of the tallest tower and the 24-hour superclub from the second trailer.
LAND.np: Light trails on the boulevard and the tower crowns changing color: downtown at its most cinematic.

LAND.name: Wynwood
LAND.p: A 25-minute walk through the murals and warehouse streets of the arts district.
LAND.np: The murals under the streetlights, with the bars and music just starting up.

LAND.name: Little Haiti
LAND.p: Caribbean color, murals and music. Stop by the cultural complex and taste a Haitian patty.

LAND.name: Little Havana
LAND.p: Cafecito and a pastelito at a ventanita, then the domino tables of Máximo Gómez Park.

LAND.name: Brickell
LAND.np: The glass towers lit up, then back over the MacArthur Causeway past the lit cruise ships to the neon of Ocean Drive.
LAND.p: The glass canyon of the financial district, then back over the MacArthur Causeway past PortMiami to Ocean Drive.

WATER.name: Bayside Marina
WATER.p: Board under the downtown towers, with the arena and the waterfront right behind you.

WATER.name: PortMiami
WATER.p: Cruise past the giant cruise ships and cargo cranes of the world’s busiest cruise port.

WATER.name: Fisher Island
WATER.p: The island with no road: reachable only by boat or ferry, and home to some of the most expensive real estate in the US.

WATER.name: Miami Beach Marina
WATER.p: Superyachts lined up at the south end of Miami Beach, near South Pointe.

WATER.name: Star Island
WATER.p: The heart of Millionaire’s Row: celebrity mansions with private docks, one after another.

WATER.name: Palm & Hibiscus Islands
WATER.p: Palm-lined estates along the MacArthur Causeway, including the island where Al Capone once owned a waterfront house.

WATER.name: Venetian Islands
WATER.p: Weave between the islands and under the old drawbridge causeway.

WATER.name: Downtown & Brickell skyline
WATER.p: Engines off mid-bay for the golden-hour skyline shot, then back to Bayside.
